sources.entry: Bookstack | Platform for organizing and storing information

summary.one_liner: BookStack is a self-described opinionated documentation platform for storing and organising information, aimed at users who only need basic word-processing skills.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes BookStack as a platform for storing and organising information and documentation, designed so new users find it intuitive with only basic word-processing skills. It states that advanced power features are available for users who want them without getting in the way of the simple core experience. The README does not list specific features such as page or book structure, editors, or permissions. It points to external docs, an installation guide, a demo instance, and a community forum for details. The project is MIT-licensed and lists many third-party libraries (Laravel, TinyMCE, Lexical, CodeMirror, and others) used to build it. Translations are managed through Crowdin, and development work happens on the development branch.
use_cases: store company information in one place
collaborate on documentation with non-technical staff
how_to_run: See the Installation Instructions on the official BookStack website (linked from the README; no commands given in the README).
notable: Opinionated design focused on a simple out-of-the-box experience for basic word-processing users
Translations managed through Crowdin, with contributions made there rather than by pull request
Supports SAML and OAuth2 client libraries among its dependencies
Stable upgrade path with a relaxed, open development philosophy
Not designed as an extensible platform for purposes beyond documentation
caveats: The README states it is not designed to be an extensible platform for purposes outside documentation
Installation details are only on the external website, not in the README
Accessibility aims at WCAG 2.1 Level A where possible but are not strictly tested each release
